title: Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2018-26-01 for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. AD 2018- 26-01 required initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. Since the FAA issued AD 2018-26-01, CFM issued updated service material providing improvements to the ultrasonic inspection procedures and expanding the inspection area. This AD requires initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Model H160-B helicopters. This AD was prompted by a determination that a gap without fire-resistant sealant (sealant) may be present in the cargo bay near the fuel segregation box. This AD requires inspecting for any missing sealant and, depending on findings, corrective action. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Bell Textron Canada Limited Helicopters
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bell Textron Canada Limited (Bell) Model 429 helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of premature wear-out of certain spherical bearings due to a quality escape of the spherical bearing monoballs not receiving the required hard coating. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the tail rotor (TR) pitch link assemblies and their bearings for cracks, wear, and mechanical or corrosion damage and, depending on the results, replacing any affected TR pitch link assembly. This AD also allows an affected part to be installed in a helicopter if certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-08-06 which applied to certain Airbus Helicopters Model SA330J helicopters. AD 2025-08-06 required repetitively inspecting for a gap between the main gearbox (MGB) oil cooling fan assembly rotor blade and the upper section of the guide vane bearing housing, replacing the MGB fan rotor bearings with serviceable bearings if necessary, and at a later compliance time replacing the MGB fan rotor bearing assembly with an improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, which constitutes terminating action for the repetitive inspections. Since AD 2025-08-06 was issued, the FAA determined that the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly should be extended. This AD continues to require the actions in AD 2025-08-06 and increases the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly. This AD also prohibits installing any MGB fan rotor bearings and any MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Denial of Rehearing Requests by Operation of Law Under the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure
issuer: Energy Department; Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) is revising its regulations addressing the circumstances under which a request for rehearing is denied absent Commission action within a particular time frame. Currently, the Commission's regulations provide that unless the Commission acts upon a request for rehearing within 30 days after the request is filed, the request is denied. As revised in this final rule, the regulation will apply only to matters subject to the rehearing and judicial review provisions in the Federal Power Act (FPA) and Natural Gas Act (NGA).

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-21- 08, which applied to certain The Boeing Company Model 737-700, -700C, - 800, and -900ER series airplanes. AD 2026-21-08 required a detailed inspection of the left- and right-side form-in-place (FiP) gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panels for any leak, and applicable on-condition actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-21-08, the FAA has determined that the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of AD 2026-21-08 omits reference to a certain date. This AD retains all of the requirements of AD 2026- 21-08 and adds the omitted reference to the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of this AD. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Employee or Independent Contractor Status Under the Fair Labor Standards Act, Family and Medical Leave Act, and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act
issuer: Labor Department; Wage and Hour Division
summary: This final rule rescinds the analysis for determining employee or independent contractor status under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA or Act) set forth in the Department of Labor's (Department) regulations and replaces it with an analysis similar to what it published in a final rule promulgated in 2021, with several modifications and enhancements. In addition, this final rule amends provisions in the Department's regulations implementing the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act (MSPA) to provide that employee or independent contractor status under those laws should be determined using the Department's FLSA analysis, as the FMLA and MSPA both incorporate the FLSA's scope of employment.

title: Horse Protection Amendments; Extension of Postponement of Regulations
issuer: Agriculture Department; Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service
summary: On May 8, 2024, we published a final rule amending the horse protection regulations. The final rule was initially scheduled to go into effect on February 1, 2025, except for Sec. 11.19, which was effective on June 7, 2024. On January 28, 2025, we published a postponement of the effective date of the remaining provisions from February 1, 2025, to April 2, 2025. On March 21, 2025, we published a further delay of the effective date to February 1, 2026, and a request for comment on whether the length of the postponement should be extended. On January 28, 2026, based on developments following the issuance of the March 21, 2025, delay of effective date, we published a document further delaying the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2026. On November 13, 2026, we published a proposed rule to remove parts of the 2024 Horse Protection final rule that were vacated by Court order from the regulations, as well as proposing to withdraw the non-vacated parts and update the regulations. As a consequence, in this document, we are issuing an extension of the postponement of the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2027.
